title: Granule cells reorient cortical trajectories to separate contexts.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad API metadata for doi:10.5061/dryad.9p8cz8x0p (version 4, CC0, 10,661,937,620 bytes total). File listing: data1.mat 1.49 GB, data2.mat 2.29 GB, data3.mat 3.09 GB, data4.mat 3.76 GB, optodata.mat 26.8 MB, README.md 24.7 kB. Tried to download README.md: Dryad API returned 401 and the web file stream sits behind a bot-check page (proof-of-work challenge, not a login), so no file was opened. From the bioRxiv preprint full text (PMC12991086): '18 sessions from 9 mice', about 123 Reach and 128 VR trials per session.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Contents of the .mat files (reward-aligned behaviour, licking, L5PT (layer 5 pyramidal tract) and GrC (granule cell) fluorescence, cell registration, trial metadata) come from the Dryad abstract only. The cohort structure (18 trained cross-task pairs, 9 novice pairs, 9 same-task control pairs) also comes from the Dryad abstract. Neuron counts per session were not found.

a1_downloadable.note: CC0 on Dryad with no login or application; a browser can download it. Automated download was blocked by a bot-check page, so this was not verified.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Task context (Reach vs VR) and trial phase are probably in the trial metadata, according to the Dryad abstract. Not verified. These are design variables the experimenter set, not measured outcomes.

a3_inputs_present.note: Fluorescence traces are said to be stored directly in the .mat files (Dryad abstract), so no identifier lookups are needed. Not opened.

a4_units_stated.note: The Dryad abstract says the README documents 'variable definitions, dimensions, units'. The README could not be retrieved.

a5_enough_rows.note: The independent unit is the mouse or session: 9 trained mice and 18 cross-task session pairs (preprint), with about 125 trials per task per session. Any honest split must hold out whole mice, which leaves about 9 groups. That is far below the threshold, whatever the trial count (about 4,500 trials, estimated but not counted).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 10.7 GB total across four MATLAB .mat files of 1.5 to 3.8 GB each
a6_fits_laptop.note: The full working set is over 5 GB. One file might load lazily if it is HDF5-based MATLAB v7.3, but the internal layout is unverified.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not checkable without opening the files. The cohort counts in the Dryad abstract (18 trained pairs) match the preprint's '18 sessions from 9 mice'.

a8_label_provenance.note: Context labels are the experimental design, not a model output. Note that the calcium signals themselves are extracted by cNMF (constrained non-negative matrix factorization) from the raw imaging.

honest_claim_h3: Within 9 mice from one lab, a decoder can separate Reach from VR context in granule-cell activity better than in cortical activity, which restates the paper's own analysis rather than giving a new predictive claim.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use cortical neuron activity to predict cerebellar granule cell activity and task context across two learned motor skills in mice.
plain_idea.train_on: Trial-aligned calcium imaging traces from premotor cortex output neurons and cerebellar granule cells, recorded simultaneously. There are 18 session pairs from 9 trained mice and about 125 trials per task per session; exact neuron and trial counts were not verified.
plain_idea.predict: Which task the mouse is doing (forelimb reach vs virtual-reality running), or granule cell activity from cortical activity. The true task label is set by the experimental design.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Cerebellar systems neuroscientists would learn whether a cortex-to-cerebellum mapping generalizes across contexts. However, the paper already answers this with low-dimensional analyses, and 9 mice cannot support a held-out-animal model.

ml_idea: Decode task context, or predict granule cell population activity from simultaneously imaged cortical output neurons, with a split that holds out whole mice. This is not viable: there are only 9 mice, neurons are not matched across animals, the deposit is 10.7 GB of MATLAB files, and no CPU-friendly frozen backbone exists for calcium imaging.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated, because Part A failed. Sizes come from the Dryad file listing.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct mice in the trial metadata: 9 trained mice (preprint) is already the kill.

verdict_reason: A5 fails: the independent unit is the mouse (9 trained mice, 18 session pairs), so a held-out-animal evaluation has about 9 groups. A6 also fails: 10.7 GB of MATLAB files that a bot check stopped me from opening. The obvious prediction targets are design variables the paper already analyses, not measured outcomes to learn.
